item.title: Enterprise architecture
item.description:
Enterprise architecture is the practice that tries to describe and control an organisation’s structure, processes, applications, systems, and technology in an integrated way.

The word “tries” does a lot of work in that sentence. Most organisations never actually achieve integration. They accumulate systems, outgrow their documentation, and hire someone to draw boxes and arrows.

item.title: Enterprise Architecture Model
item.description:
An architecture model is not just useful to provide insight into the current or future situation; it can also be used to evaluate the transition from ‘as is’ to ’to be’.

The hard part is mapping the gap between where you are and where you want to be, and being honest about which parts of the journey are actually feasible.

item.title: Enterprise Architecture is the structure and the operational blueprint of a company
item.description:
Enterprise Architecture is the structure and the operational blueprint of a company.

It’s the difference between a building that holds things together and one that collapses the first time the wind picks up. You don’t notice it when it’s done well. You notice it the moment it’s missing.

item.title: Archimate
item.description:
Archimate is an open and independent enterprise architecture modelling language that enables organisations to communicate, design, analyse and manage their enterprise architecture in a visual way.

It provides a comprehensive and consistent modelling language to describe, visualise, analyse and validate the architecture of an enterprise. The language is developed and maintained by The Open Group, the same body behind TOGAF.

The key idea is that enterprise architecture isn’t just about IT systems. It spans business processes, applications, technology infrastructure, and the people and motivations that drive it all. Archimate gives you a common vocabulary across all of those layers so that a business architect, an application architect, and a technology architect can all be talking about the same thing.
